title: Human tau pathology is associated with lonely, nontraveling slow waves linked to memory impairment
title_zh: 人类tau病理与孤独、不旅行的慢波有关，这种慢波与记忆障碍相关
abstract: Memory markedly declines with age, exaggerated in those with Alzheimer’s disease, yet the mechanisms are still not resolved. Here we show that frontal lobe tau pathology in humans is associated with impaired en masse unity and cortical traveling propagation of nonrapid eye movement slow waves, linked to impaired memory retention. We elucidate these findings using positron-emission tomography tau brain imaging, and then replicate and extend them using Alzheimer’s disease pathology markers derived from cerebrospinal fluid in an independent clinical cohort. Thus, tau-associated memory deficits are not wholly direct but indirectly linked to consequential ‘lonely’, nontraveling slow-wave events. Frontal cortical tau pathology in aging humans is associated with reduced slow-wave travel during sleep. This reduced propagation is associated with poorer overnight memory retention, supporting a link between slow-wave travel and age-related memory function.
abstract_zh: 随着年龄增长，记忆力显著下降，阿尔茨海默病患者更为严重，但其机制尚未完全阐明。在此，我们展示了人类额叶tau病理与非快速眼动睡眠慢波群体统一性和皮层旅行传播受损有关，这与记忆巩固受损相关。我们通过正电子发射断层扫描tau脑成像阐明了这些发现，随后利用脑脊液中阿尔茨海默病病理标志物在独立的临床队列中复制并延伸了这些发现。因此，与tau相关的记忆缺陷并非完全直接，而是间接与关键的‘孤独’、不旅行的慢波事件相关。衰老人类的额叶tau病理与睡眠期间慢波传播减少有关。这种传播减少与过夜记忆保持能力较差相关，支持慢波旅行与衰老相关记忆功能之间的联系。
